responses.evidence: B-09 now carries the persistence obligation on the stage's own entry point, taking the clear condition's first route. Its `then` adds "exactly one AUDIT_UNCHANGED entry for the slice's GitHub issue was recorded through recordSelfAuditOutcome (B-10) before the stage returned, with candidateTreeId and auditedTreeId both equal to that released tree id", and its observableResult declares the observation that fails on violation: "selfAuditsFor(loadRunState(<that temporary run-state directory>), ghIssue) returns exactly one entry whose verdict is \"AUDIT_UNCHANGED\" and whose candidateTreeId and auditedTreeId both equal the released checkpoint tree id — so a stage that classifies AUDIT_UNCHANGED and never calls the writer fails here, which a src/run-state.test.ts writer round-trip cannot do". The harness is the one the finding identified as already declared: B-02's temporary run-state directory and its selfAuditsFor(loadRunState(...)) read against the same stage entry point, so no new seam and no spawned scenario is added. The contract's B-09 statement and the matching test-plan scenario carry the same claim, the scenario ending "A stage that classifies AUDIT_UNCHANGED without calling recordSelfAuditOutcome fails this scenario." B-10 keeps its stable ID, its schema shape, its version bump, its reader and writer, and the three literal-6 pins, but no longer asserts the stage-level claim it could not fail on: its statement now reads that it round-trips writer against reader "while the obligation that a classifying stage actually calls it the moment the verdict lands is B-09's, observed there on the stage's own entry point so that an unreferenced writer cannot pass". The scope lock is aligned to the same reading: "on an identical tree the stage itself records AUDIT_UNCHANGED in run state (schema v7) before it returns". The Definition of done line the finding quoted is unchanged and now has an observation behind it. A candidate that ships recordSelfAuditOutcome unreferenced therefore fails B-09's tests and acceptance:behaviors.

Taken by the clear condition's second route, which is the one this repo's own decisions point at: B-03's scan is left as a pure source-order assertion rather than extended into the injected callback's body, because pinning an anchor inside that body is the same stale-syntax class #299's operator decision (2026-09-14, part 1) refused when it rejected extending the scan into the QA argument list, and #300 rebuilds that dispatch site. The contract now states the limitation and names what exercises it. B-03's contract statement adds: "No declared observation in this slice binds that argument to a real generator invocation in the candidate worktree — with --self-audit default off and a new spawned pipeline scenario an explicit non-goal, the orchestrator-to-provider wiring is carried by pnpm run typecheck accepting the callback's type and by nothing else. It is first exercised for real by an operator self-run launched with --self-audit, whose audit outcomes become readable through the run-summary totals and status surfaces #301 owns; #300 is the sibling slice that builds the changed-tree path over the same injected dispatch. Stated deliberately so no candidate reads the stage's dispatch-spy tests as coverage of the wiring." B-09's ADR 0002 / ADR 0007 sentence now closes with "That sentence is carried by pnpm run typecheck alone in this slice; B-03 records why and names what exercises it later." Both manifest observableResults (B-03, B-09) carry the same statement, and the test-plan scan scenario ends "The scan asserts nothing about the injected dispatch argument: that the callback reaches a real generator invocation is proven only by pnpm run typecheck here, and no test in this slice claims otherwise."
